selection.ownership: Cloudflare, Inc., San Francisco, California, United States. Reviewed edition is the international Cloudflare product, not a mainland-China operator.

research.searchCoverage: Official Cloudflare API MCP (Code Mode) at https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp with OAuth at mcp.cloudflare.com/authorize and Bearer API tokens, tools docs/search/execute, pinned OpenConnector withMcpClient streamable HTTP, Cloudflare Inc. San Francisco identity, and dated incident search for Cloudflare MCP / Cloudflare API security breach reviewed on 2026-09-13. Historical Cloudbleed (2017), Okta/Atlassian (2022), Salesloft Drift (2025-08), and availability incidents are recorded. Native templates cannot express MCP sessions, SSE, or OAuth dynamic client registration. This is not a breach-free claim.

Cloudflare API MCP is the official Code Mode server at mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp. Official auth is OAuth (mcp.cloudflare.com/authorize + /token, PKCE S256, tokenEndpointAuthMethod none) or Authorization Bearer API token. Pinned source uses MCP streamable HTTP listTools/callTool. Native REST templates cannot express MCP or that OAuth shape. Host is bounded. No current unresolved MCP compromise identified on 2026-09-13.

incidents.finding: Cloudbleed: a Cloudflare HTML parser buffer overflow leaked memory (cookies, tokens, POST bodies) across customer traffic. Disclosed by Google Project Zero. Cloudflare patched the parser and reported no evidence of malicious exploitation.
incidents.limitation: Historical 2017 parser bug under the 2026-09-13 waiver. Not a current unresolved Cloudflare API compromise.

incidents.finding: Cloudflare investigated the January 2022 Okta compromise affecting its Atlassian environment. Cloudflare stated production systems serving customer traffic were not impacted.
incidents.limitation: Historical third-party identity-vendor incident. Not a current unresolved Email Routing / R2 / MCP API compromise.

incidents.finding: Salesloft Drift campaign accessed Cloudflare's Salesforce tenant (support-ticket data) between 2025-08-12 and 2025-08-17. Cloudflare stated no Cloudflare services or infrastructure were compromised.
incidents.limitation: Historical third-party SaaS exposure. Not an api.cloudflare.com customer-token compromise. 2026-09-13 waiver keeps historical non-China incidents.

incidents.finding: R2 Gateway was inadvertently disabled during abuse remediation, causing a 59-minute R2 API availability outage. Cloudflare reported no loss or corruption of stored R2 data.
incidents.limitation: Historical availability incident, not a credential or data-exfiltration compromise.
